faults.quote: Before any data: you've framed revenue and cost as two sides, but your revenue branch already assumes the drop is volume or price.
faults.why: The candidate asked directly for departures, average fare and the operating-cost split. The interviewer gave no release, refusal or deferral, only a vague 'before any data'. The cost-split ask was never addressed directly.

faults.quote: Hub–Port Avery shows the same pattern: 80 seats, a 75% load factor and $20 of extras per passenger, with variable cost of $11,000 per flight in both years, while the average fare fell from $240 to $160.
faults.why: The candidate asked for the network-wide ticket/ancillary split and departure counts. The interviewer instead released one route's per-flight economics, which is analysis-stage data. This revealed the contested-route fare collapse during the structure phase.

faults.quote: I don't have the ticket versus extras revenue split.
faults.why: The extras_revenue item ($20 per passenger in both years) answers this coarsely, and with flat volume the split is derivable. The $20 extras figure appeared in the same turn's Port Avery line.

faults.quote: what is the biggest risk that this plan still ends the year in a loss?
faults.why: The candidate had just named a risk (a competitor following into Ashford), and the interviewer asked for the risk again in the same turn as a separate walk-through question.
